   921	    def change_aliases(self, change_map):
   922	        """
   923	        Change the aliases in change_map (which maps old-alias -> new-alias),
   924	        relabelling any references to them in select columns and the where
   925	        clause.
   926	        """

   928	        # updated twice (e.g. T4 -> T5, T5 -> T6, so also T4 -> T6) depending
   929	        # on their order in change_map.
   930	        assert set(change_map).isdisjoint(change_map.values())

   966	    def bump_prefix(self, other_query, exclude=None):
   967	        """
   968	        Change the alias prefix to the next letter in the alphabet in a way
   969	        that the other query's aliases and this query's aliases will not
   970	        conflict. Even tables that previously had no alias will get an alias
   971	        after this call. To prevent changing aliases use the exclude parameter.

   974	        def prefix_gen():
   975	            """
   976	            Generate a sequence of characters in alphabetical order:
   977	                -> 'A', 'B', 'C', ...
   978	
   979	            When the alphabet is finished, the sequence will continue with the
   980	            Cartesian product:
   981	                -> 'AA', 'AB', 'AC', ...
   982	            """
   983	            alphabet = ascii_uppercase
   984	            prefix = chr(ord(self.alias_prefix) + 1)
   985	            yield prefix
   986	            for n in count(1):
   987	                seq = alphabet[alphabet.index(prefix) :] if prefix else alphabet

   989	                    yield "".join(s)
